feat(ingestion): 10-K Item section parser with profile-driven segmentation

SEC fixes what a 10-K contains (Part/Item) but not how it is laid out in
HTML. The parser keeps per-company layout knowledge as data (profiles) and
lets a single `segmentation.type` select the parsing strategy, so parsing
stays deterministic with no LLM in the loop.

- parser.py: normalize -> blockize -> segment -> validate -> ParsedFiling
- xref.py: page-join strategy for filings with no Item headings in the body
  (Intel), using the SEC-mandated Cross-Reference Index
- validation-driven fallback: bad profiles are never persisted
- 20/20 filings parse with zero warnings; 309 tests
- docs/m1/: findings, spec, build, bugs, verify
- scripts/check_doc_code.py: doc code blocks are anchored to source symbols
  and verified in pytest, so docs cannot drift from the code

Drops the LLM profile experiment (llm_profile.py, bench_llm_profile.py):
the A/B run showed the model could map titles to Items but not derive the
CSS rules covering them, so rule derivation stays in code.

author: Sungyong Cho <dev@sungyongcho.com> 1786552239 +0200
message:
feat(ingestion): render 10-K tables as markdown (M1.2)

The hard part is not serialization, it is layout. Measured over this corpus's
1,200 table blocks: 64% of cells are empty, <th> never appears at all, and
colspan is used 57,617 times purely to position text. A three-column income
statement ships as twelve physical columns of label / value / unit / spacer.
Converting that straight to markdown yields a wide, mostly-empty grid that is
worse for retrieval than the raw text.

So layout is collapsed before anything is serialized:

  to_grid            colspan/rowspan -> dense matrix
  drop_empty         drop empty rows and columns   221,730 -> 66,575 cells (30%)
  merge_unit_columns fold '$'/'%'-only columns into their value
  split_header       infer header rows, since there is no <th> to read
  to_markdown        serialize

Two decisions worth recording:

Block.text is left alone. The planned contract was to fill it with markdown,
but the parser emits Block("table", "", html=...) and the coverage metric sums
len(b.text), so filling it would have shifted all 20 coverage goldens. Keeping
this a pure function over HTML means table rendering cannot move that metric
and the parser stays unaware of markdown; the chunker calls it in M1.3.

Parenthesized negatives stay verbatim: (1,234) is not rewritten to -1234. The
citation has to match what a reader sees in the filing, and normalizing at
ingest is irreversible while normalizing at query time is not.

33 tests; the suite goes 309 -> 342. tables_mine.py plus the TABLES_MODULE
switch keep the reimplement-it-yourself path working (1 passed, 32 skipped on
an empty stub).

feat: local model providers for embeddings and reranking

Fill the two provider boundaries M2 designed but never implemented.

- app/retrieval/sbert.py: SentenceTransformerEmbeddingProvider, a local
  bi-encoder behind EmbeddingProvider. Defaults to all-MiniLM-L6-v2, whose

  RerankProvider boundary with a model that reads query and document together.
- service.retrieve gains an optional reranker. Without one the M2.7 behaviour
  is unchanged; with one, fusion keeps the full candidate pool and the
  reranker rescores it down to k.

  declared as a uv conflict set so only one backend installs. CPU is the
  default; these models are too small for an accelerator to pay off.

stays importable with no torch backend installed. Vectors from different
providers do not share a space, so switching requires re-embedding.

author: Sungyong Cho <dev@sungyongcho.com> 1787590582 +0200
message:
feat(retrieval): complete M2.9-M2.11 checkpoints

M2.9 adds BM25 as a selectable alternative to the ts_rank_cd lexical
baseline. Term frequencies, document lengths, and document frequencies are
derived from chunks.content_tsv rather than recomputed in Python, so the
statistics agree with PostgreSQL's own tokenizer by construction instead of
by coincidence. The rebuild is explicit and total: it is derived data, and a
partial refresh is worth less than none.

Both published idf variants are selectable. Lucene's ln(1 + ratio) is the
default because Robertson's original goes negative once a lexeme appears in
more than half the corpus, which on a small corpus inverts the ranking
outright. df is clamped to the corpus size so stale statistics cannot make
Robertson take a logarithm of a nonpositive number.

M2.10 and M2.11 keep their local-model providers behind a lazy import so
app.retrieval stays importable without a torch backend extra, and their
tests use fake encoders so neither downloads weights.

ts_rank_cd remains the production default. Fusion consumes ranks, not
scores, so the two rankers stay comparable without normalizing BM25 against
cover density.

author: Sungyong Cho <dev@sungyongcho.com> 1787591077 +0200
message:
feat(evals): compare PostgreSQL lexical rankers

The M3 matrix now crosses chunk target by retrieval path by lexical ranker,
producing ten arms instead of six. The ranker axis crosses only the paths
that actually issue a lexical query: crossing it with vector as well would
run the same retrieval twice and write two artifacts differing only in a
label neither arm used, so vector stays at one arm per chunk target.

Every arm carries its ranker in its name, in its artifact filename, and in
its JSON provenance. Two runs of the same chunking and strategy under
different rankers can no longer overwrite each other or be mistaken for one
another after the fact.

BM25 statistics are rebuilt once per corpus arm, inside the temporary
corpus that owns them. df, avgdl, and dl are all properties of a particular
chunking, so a rebuild shared across chunk targets would describe neither.
The rebuild happens during indexing, before any experiment runs, which is
also where its cost belongs in the indexing budget.

The query budget uses the first ranker the caller named so that a budget
number always identifies the path it measured.

author: Sungyong Cho <dev@sungyongcho.com> 1787596113 +0200
message:
fix(retrieval): stop the lexical baseline requiring every query term

websearch_to_tsquery joins every content lexeme with AND, so the golden
question "What was the total revenue reported for fiscal 2024?" only
matched a chunk containing all five stems. On the real corpus that is no
chunk at all: every committed evaluation of the lexical arm recorded
recall@5 = 0.000 with zero hits across all 28 cases, and nothing raised,
because an empty result set is not an error.

The statement now relaxes the parsed query before using it. The tsquery's
text form quotes each lexeme and never contains "&" inside one, so
rewriting "&" to "|" and reparsing with to_tsquery turns the conjunction
into a disjunction while leaving quoted phrases (<->) intact. The raw
query stays a bound parameter throughout.

Matching alone was not enough. With ts_rank_cd's default normalization the
rank degenerates into occurrence counting, and chunks stuffed with one
ubiquitous term ("AMD", "fiscal") beat the chunk that answers: recall
stayed 0.000 even with candidates. A sweep of every normalization bitmask
against the golden suite picked 4|1 - divide by the mean harmonic distance
between extents, then by 1 + log(length) - which prefers chunks where more
of the query co-occurs closely. One semantic is knowingly weakened: an
explicit -term exclusion is relaxed along with everything else.

Measured on the 1200-char corpus (recall@5 / MRR):
  lexical ts_rank_cd  0.000 / 0.000  ->  0.271 / 0.172
  hybrid  ts_rank_cd  0.063 / 0.083  ->  0.104 / 0.097
  BM25 arms unchanged (0.521 / 0.395), still the stronger ranker.

message:

The measured-evidence story predated the lexical fix and the BM25 arm: the
README and the evaluation report still said the best Recall@5 was 0.125
and that lexical retrieval returned no candidates, which stopped being
true of this code the moment M2.9 landed. A repository whose central claim

The committed 20260824T203336Z artifacts record the full ten-arm matrix
with 200 budget queries. Headlines: BM25 lexical at 1200 characters leads
with Recall@5 0.521 / MRR 0.395; the relaxed ts_rank_cd baseline retrieves
at 0.271-0.333 where it previously measured zero, paying for its recall
with the widest candidate sets and the slowest P95s; and plain lexical
beats hybrid everywhere, because rank-only RRF cannot know the
deterministic vector component is weak and fusing it in dilutes a stronger
ranking. The six-arm predecessor stays committed as the record that
motivated the fix, and the failure analysis now points from the diagnosis
to the remeasurement.

The production default stays ts_rank_cd. Promoting BM25 is an author
decision the report explicitly declines to automate.

  leave the package init carrying nothing but its docstring

  trace contracts require

message:
fix(admin): keep the job ledger consistent when progress writes race or fail

Summary
An ingest finished in memory but stayed `running` in the ledger, which stalled the queue until a restart. Progress writes were fire-and-forget tasks that could land after the terminal write, hold pooled connections in bursts, and take the worker down with them.

Changes

- `ProgressPersister` in `app/operator/jobs.py`: one write in flight per job, a single catch-up write for snapshots that arrive mid-write, a terminal write that waits for in-flight progress and retries transient failures, and logging instead of raising
- corpus and evaluation services route progress and terminal writes through it; the worker loop records a `worker_error` failure instead of dying on an unexpected exception
- offline tests for coalescing, ordering, retry, and a flaky in-memory ledger

message:
feat(llm): give the local engine one assembly path and a production kill switch

Summary
Protocol resolution and the zero-cost budget move into one module both surfaces call, the request timeout and token budgets become configurable, and MODE=prod disables the local engine whatever the environment says.

Changes

- `app/llm/local_engine.py`: `resolve_local_protocol`, `local_provider_budget` and `build_local_provider`, replacing the copy of each in the runtime API and the release app. The release path had been borrowing the OpenAI token limits for a local model that is usually much smaller
- `app/llm/local.py`: the HTTP timeout is a constructor argument instead of a hardcoded 30 seconds, and the default rises to 120. Structured output from a CPU-hosted model over a full evidence prompt does not finish in 30 seconds, so every local review was dying as a read timeout
- Settings: `LOCAL_LLM_TIMEOUT_S`, `LOCAL_LLM_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` and `LOCAL_LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` are readable from the environment on both classes, and a blank Compose substitution falls back to the field default rather than failing to parse
- `local_llm_enabled` becomes the single gate on both settings classes and now requires a non-production environment, so a published build cannot answer from an unvetted local model even if a stray variable reaches it. Readiness reports `disabled_in_prod` and issues no probe
- The shared default timeout lives in `app/settings_sources.py` so reading configuration never drags the OpenAI SDK into the process

Verification

- ruff check, ruff format --check: pass; pytest -m "not live_postgres": 1516 passed, 1 skipped; npm test: 139 passed
- Mutation checks: removing the production term from either settings class, dropping the readiness reason, or losing the timeout argument each fails a test

message:
feat(compose): split the stack into a development and a production layer

Summary
A shared base gains two overlays. Development adds the local model engine and an opt-in Ollama host; production reproduces what a visitor sees and cannot reach a local model at all.

Changes

- `docker-compose.dev.yml`: forwards every `LOCAL_LLM_*` key and adds an `ollama` service behind the `local-llm` profile, with a named volume for the weights, a pinned tag, no published port and nothing depending on it, so the default topology and `docker compose config` are unchanged when it is absent
- `docker-compose.prod.yml`: bakes the public web bundle, selects the production key slot and the read-only administrator mode. Together with the settings guard the local engine is impossible here twice over
- `docker-compose.yml` keeps only the shared topology; the local model keys move out, so the production layer has no such variable to forward
- The VM deployment file moves to `deploy/gcp/docker-compose.deploy.yml`, beside the script that copies it, and that script and the deployment notes follow
- `scripts/verify_clean_checkout.sh` unsets every `LOCAL_LLM_*` variable, which was the one remaining way a developer's shell could leak into a clean run, and validates both overlays
- `.env.example` documents the layering through `COMPOSE_FILE`, so plain `docker compose up` still means development, and replaces the bridge-gateway advice with the profile recipe

Verification

- ruff check, ruff format --check: pass; pytest -m "not live_postgres": 1523 passed, 1 skipped; npm test: 139 passed; typecheck, check_web_build.py, git diff --check: pass
- `docker compose config` on each layer: base and production resolve to db plus app with no local keys, development adds them, and the profile adds ollama only when asked

message:

Summary
A failed run says what went wrong instead of printing its status code, and the review workspace and the Playground now read the same failure the same way.

- A timeout and a refused connection are distinguished, since one means raise the deadline and the other means the model host is not running. A schema rejection says so and, where relevant, that smaller local models often fail structured output
- Advice a reader cannot act on is withheld from a public build, so it never sees a variable name or a compose profile
- The Playground stops formatting failures its own way

author: Sungyong Cho <dev@sungyongcho.com> 1788350841 +0200
message:
fix(llm): ask Ollama for a context window that matches the budget

Summary
Three defects found by running the local engine for real: a truncated model context, an image tag too old to pull current models, and a status panel whose columns collided.

Changes

- The Ollama request now sends `num_ctx` covering both halves of the provider budget. Ollama otherwise loads the model with its own default window, commonly 4096 tokens, and silently drops the overflow. Verified against a running host: the model previously loaded at 4096 while the budget claimed 28,000, so the evidence prompt was being cut without a word. An answer about filings the model never read is the one failure this system must not hide
- The pinned Ollama image moves to a release recent enough to pull current models. The earlier pin refused their manifests with a 412 telling the reader to upgrade
- The local model policy panel gives each row its own line for the explanation instead of competing for width with the model name, and no longer forces three equal status columns

Verification

- pytest -m "not live_postgres": 1524 passed, 1 skipped; npm test: 150 passed; typecheck, check_web_build.py, ruff, git diff --check: pass
- Mutation check: dropping the explicit window fails a test
- On a running host the model now loads at exactly the requested window, and the panel renders without overlap
